pageDispositions.notes: Title page: Introduction to Deep Reinforcement Learning. Printed footer 1. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.
Objectives roadmap: neural approximation, DQN networks, exploration, navigation case and training challenges. Printed footer 2. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

RL/deep-learning Venn diagram and sequential decision definition inspected. Tabular RL is the contrast, not all classical RL; finite-output DQN does not automatically handle continuous actions. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Full agent/action/environment/next-state-reward loop and tabular Q-learning equation inspected. Deterministic policy notation is one case; terminal bootstrap handling is unstated. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Large state/action tables and lack of direct parameter sharing inspected. Tabular limitations concern representation and sample demands, not categorical inability to handle changing environments. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Actual 3×3 grid and three-row four-action Q table inspected. Nine positions and four actions give 36 entries; Down is greedy in each displayed row. Dynamic-obstacle claims require state/Markov and sample-demand qualifications. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Fetch illustration, 8³=512 state bins and six actions giving 3,072 entries inspected. Position encoding omits other physical information. Deep approximation is motivated, not the only possible non-tabular method. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Q-table-to-neural-approximator figure inspected. Text describes scalar state-action input while figure uses state-only input with three action outputs; these are different valid architectures, not identical input contracts. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Actual network has three inputs, two hidden layers of four and four outputs. Feature prose lists four scalars, so the schematic is not a literal match. Fully connected architecture gives 44 weights, plus 12 biases if explicitly assumed. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Corridor diagram and Q table inspected: distances 4.8, 0.6 and 0.2 m favor Forward, Turn and Stop respectively. Q values are not probabilities. No weights are supplied to compute the exact unseen 3.14 m output. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

MLP/vector, CNN/image and RNN/history examples inspected. These are suitable examples, not exclusive architectures or guarantees of observability. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Policy, value and model function list inspected. P(s′|s,a) is a transition model; reward prediction requires a separate or joint reward model. Theta convention includes trainable parameters, typically biases as well as weights. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Four-family table inspected: direct policy, action value, dynamics and combined actor/critic. REINFORCE, SARSA/DQN, Dyna-Q/MCTS and A2C/PPO are examples; not every named algorithm is inherently deep or learns a model. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Value-based description and SARSA on-policy versus DQN off-policy inspected. V(s) is not itself an action-indexed value; model/lookahead is needed to compare actions from state values alone. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Full RL plus DNN → Q-vector → exploration-policy diagram inspected. The Q-network scores actions; epsilon-greedy/Boltzmann selects actions. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Atari image/CNN/action-output diagram inspected. Five illustrated actions are schematic, not a validated Breakout action set. Greedy selection is exploitation, not the entire exploration policy. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Main network acting and training-prediction roles inspected. Theta is optimized through the chosen-action loss; identical architecture does not mean identical weights at every step. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Target-network equation y=r+gamma max Q(s′,a′;phi), hard copying and beta-retention soft update inspected. Terminal handling and update schedule require explicit assumptions. Frozen targets mitigate, not guarantee avoidance of, instability. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Two-action example inspected: main Left2.1/Right4.3, greedy Right, reward+1. Fixed target parameters have a different role from action selection. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Next-state target values Left3/Right5, gamma0.9 and target5.5 inspected. Main prediction4.3 implies TD error1.2. Exact neural-output change needs network gradient/optimizer context. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Epsilon-greedy and Boltzmann softmax equation inspected. Uniform random actions may include the greedy action; positive temperature and tie conventions must be stated. Q-to-probability transformation is distinct from raw Q. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Static, predictable dynamic and unpredictable dynamic table inspected. Categories depend on the modeled motion during the episode, not merely whether the object is a person or furniture. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Mobile wheel speeds0.42/0.51m/s, arm torques1.8/−0.6N·m and drone vector inspected. Drone units are unspecified. Continuous actuators do not turn a finite-output DQN into a continuous-action optimizer. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Modified DQN with top-view RGB/CNN, inflated-robot reward and CLIK path tracking inspected. Separate planning and control roles; intended safe behavior is not a universal safety proof. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Actual concourse/home maps and legends inspected. Black static and pink dynamic obstacles; concourse12m/40cells and home9m/30cells both imply0.3m cells. Reset randomization does not mean walls move during an episode. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Actual square5×5 buffer with red center0, eight yellow1 cells and sixteen green2 cells inspected. Radius150mm is physical robot geometry, not the5×5 buffer radius. PrintedP2−50 is not universal across the next table. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

All six reward rows and both environment columns inspected. P3 is−2/−4 and P2 is−50/−2 for concourse/home; other four rows match. Aggregation and simultaneous-event priority are not specified. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Reported results text only, no tracking plots on this slide. Same model,16+16 versus8+8 and300mm minimum gap are reported simulation observations, not universal guarantees. Small tracking error alone cannot prove obstacle clearance. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.

Sample inefficiency, data-feedback instability and sparse/misaligned reward challenges inspected. Millions is an illustrative tendency, not a theorem; density alone does not imply reward hacking. Actual 1800×1013 page pixels viewed alongside extracted text.
